A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FreqKV. All 14 pages of v1 and 20 pages of v3, including their appendices, support comparison. Methods, equations, and retained experiments can be matched despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original FreqKV perplexity, LongBench, Needle-in-a-Haystack, latency, and ablation results in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds RULER, LongGenBench, larger-model evaluations, training-cost measurements, and further ablations.

M1.justification: The proposed procedure remains DCT, low-frequency retention, rescaled IDCT, and iterative cache compression with protected sink tokens and RoPE applied afterward. v1 Sections 4.2–4.3 and v3 Sections 3.3–3.4 describe the same algorithm; the rescaling component was already present in v1.

E1.justification: v3 adds RULER and LongGenBench, including extended generation from concatenated GSM8K/MMLU questions. It also introduces synonym-perturbed CNN/DailyMail inputs as a new test scenario. Existing training corpora and evaluations remain; Proof-pile moves into Appendix E rather than disappearing.

E2.justification: Compared with v1 Table 2, v3 Table 3 removes LM-Infinite and LongHeads from LongBench and adds CaM, KVMerger, LaCache, D2O, GemFilter, FastKV, and ThinK. SnapKV also joins the LLaMA-3 comparison. The LLaMA-3 Needle-in-a-Haystack evaluation gains multiple comparator methods.

E3.justification: v3 adds LLaMA-2-13B configurations, 1% retention on LongBench, and PG-19 evaluation through 256K rather than 64K. New protocols include cosine-similarity testing on 100 documents with 1% synonym replacement, a 4096-token generation limit on LongGenBench, and a controlled training-cost comparison. The established default training recipe remains substantially unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 3.2 and Appendix F add frequency-band perturbation tests, high-versus-low-frequency ablations on summarization and PG-19, mismatched training/evaluation retention ratios, sink-count ablations, and a rescaling ablation. Aggressive compression and longer extrapolation are also tested. Existing RoPE and Dropping analyses are retained.

E5.justification: v1 Section 6.2 and Table 3 report five-run latency means with standard deviations; that table is absent from v3. v3 Appendix F.2 specifies five-run averaging for retention-ratio latencies, but its main extrapolation table supplies no standard deviations or run count. This changes uncertainty reporting without establishing an increase in runs.

E6.justification: v3 adds extensive benchmark, 13B-model, ablation, training-cost, and 256K results. For example, Table 5 reports LongGenBench scores of 54.2 and 31.2 for FreqKV on GSM8K and MMLU. Existing LLaMA-3 LongBench values also change: Qasper at 50% retention changes from 42.43 to 41.60. Original 7B PG-19/Proof-pile perplexities and FLOP results remain unchanged, while the earlier Dropping latency table is removed.

T1.justification: The DCT/IDCT, attention, rescaling, and compression equations remain mathematically equivalent despite relocation, consolidation, and notation changes. v3 adds conceptual explanations and references to the Frequency Principle, but no new formal assumptions, theorems, proofs, or substantive derivations.

C1.justification: The parameter-free frequency-compression contribution remains, but the claimed empirical reach expands substantially. v3's abstract and introduction claim stable 256K extrapolation from 8K training, compared with v1's reported 64K extension, and explicitly claim improved long-generation capability alongside prefilling performance.

C2.justification: Beyond v1's energy-concentration rationale, v3 interprets low frequencies as global semantic context and high frequencies as local details. It sharpens the existing Proof-pile limitation by discussing symbol/index sensitivity, connects adaptation to the Frequency Principle, and explains retention-latency tradeoffs and progressive amplification without rescaling.

D1.justification: v3 adds a FreqKV repository link and states that supplementary material contains code. Its training-cost study specifies eight RTX6000 Ada-48GB GPUs, per-device batch size one, and eight accumulation steps, with time and memory measurements. Most previously documented training hyperparameters are retained; the PDFs do not independently verify the linked resources.

R1.justification: The introductory and related-work coverage substantially expands to ALiBi, positional interpolation, LongRoPE, recent prefilling/compression methods, and the Frequency Principle. This broadens the positioning against alternative context-extension approaches. The claim of being the first frequency-domain KV compression method for decoder-only LLMs remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are extensively rewritten around prefilling and decoding. Preliminaries are reorganized into the method section, DCT formulas move to Appendix A, and Proof-pile, retention-ratio, Dropping, and overhead discussions move into expanded appendices. The title, author information, and conference statements also change.

P2.justification: The method diagram is redrawn to show DCT, filtering, IDCT, and iterative compression. LongBench gains retention-ratio groups and averages; the perplexity table is split and gains model-size groups. Needle-in-a-Haystack panels are reorganized, the retention plot gains latency bars and a second axis, and new diagnostic plots and tables accompany the conference layout.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens support for the central method and efficiency claims. Frequency-selection and rescaling ablations test previously underexamined design choices, Table 7 directly measures training costs, and LongGenBench evaluates generation beyond v1's perplexity and understanding evidence. Broader comparisons further strengthen the evaluation. Removing the earlier latency standard deviations weakens uncertainty reporting, but this limited loss does not outweigh the substantial evidential gains.
